title: Session Stack: Trust Boundary Mapping
description: Map the VTAM → TSO → ISPF session layers. Identify where identity is bound and trust shifts.

steps.title: Connect to Mainframe
steps.screen:
Connecting to mainframe via TN3270...

Establishing LU session with VTAM.
The session fabric exists independently of TCP/IP.
steps.expected: Establish a TN3270 connection to the mainframe.
steps.hint: The session is managed by VTAM, not the network stack. Your LU session can outlive the TCP connection.

steps.title: VTAM Entry Screen
steps.screen:
z/OS V2R5   IP: 10.1.1.2

   ZZZZZZZ  /  OOOOO   SSSSS
      Z    /  O   O  S
     Z    /  O   O   SSS
    Z    /  O   O      S
   ZZZZZ /   OOOOO  SSSSS


 ===> _

F1=Help  Enter=Continue
steps.expected: Identify the VTAM session fabric — you are anonymous with no identity bound.
steps.hint: On the first connection, the Logon prompt may be missing. Press Enter and it will appear. This is the session manager itself, not a 'service on a port'.

steps.title: TSO Logon — Identity Binding
steps.screen:
TSO/E LOGON

Userid ===> HERC01
Password ===> ********

Procedure ===> IKJACCNT

Enter an 'S' before each option:
  -Nomail  -Nonotice  -Reconnect
steps.expected: Log in to TSO to bind identity. VTAM routes the session to TSO, RACF verifies the password.
steps.hint: VTAM acts as a session router. The transition from VTAM to TSO is a control-plane boundary crossing. There is no root user — RACF distributes authority across profiles.

steps.title: Enter RFE (ISPF)
steps.screen:
READY

rfe

 RFE - MVS 3.8j Turnkey System

Option ===>_

0  Settings     1  Browse      2  Edit
3  Utilities    4  Foreground  5  Batch
6  Command      7  Dialog      8  LM

F1=Help  F3=Exit
steps.expected: Enter RFE (ISPF-like interface). Your TSO address space persists — identity context survives across panels.
steps.hint: Type RFE at the READY prompt. TK5 uses RFE, not modern ISPF. There is no SDSF panel — job output is viewed via TSO commands.

steps.title: ISPF Utilities — Dataset List (3.4)
steps.screen:
RFE Utility Selection Menu

Option ===> 4

1  Library      - Allocate/browse PDS
2  Dataset      - Dataset utilities
3  Move/Copy    - Move or copy datasets
4  DSLIST       - List datasets by pattern
5  Reset Stats  - Reset statistics
6  Hardcopy     - Print dataset

F1=Help  F3=Exit
steps.hint: The mainframe does not have /etc or /var. Everything is stored in datasets — cataloged, named objects with RACF profile protection.

steps.title: Browse System Datasets
steps.screen:
DSLIST - Data Sets Matching SYS1.*

Command - Enter "/" to select action
----------------------------------------------------
         SYS1.BRODCAST
         SYS1.LINKLIB          PO   U     0     32760
         SYS1.LPALIB           PO   U     0     32760
         SYS1.NUCLEUS          PO   U     0     32760
         SYS1.PARMLIB          PO   FB    80    3120
         SYS1.PROCLIB          PO   FB    80    3120

Command ===>
steps.expected: Browse SYS1 system datasets — PARMLIB, PROCLIB, LINKLIB are critical.
steps.hint: System configuration lives in datasets like SYS1.PARMLIB — not in /etc. Anyone who can UPDATE SYS1.PARMLIB can alter system behavior.

steps.title: Exit ISPF → TSO Command Line
steps.expected: Exit RFE and return to TSO READY prompt.
steps.hint: PF3 navigates back through panels. At the RFE Primary Menu, type X to exit to TSO READY. Every command at TSO READY runs under HERC01's authority — there is no sudo.

steps.title: LISTALC — Identity Context
steps.screen:
READY

LISTALC STATUS

--DDNAME   DISP
  STEPLIB
           KEEP   SYS1.CMDLIB
  SYSPROC
           KEEP   SYSC.CMDPROC
  SYSEXEC
           KEEP   SYSC.EXEC
  ISPLLIB
           KEEP   ISP.V2R2M0.ISPLOAD

READY
steps.expected: View dataset allocations — the resource context of your identity.
steps.hint: LISTALC STATUS shows every dataset allocated to this TSO session. STEPLIB, ISPTLIB control which programs and panels are available. These allocations were established at logon.

steps.title: Logoff — Return to VTAM
steps.screen:
READY

LOGOFF

IKJ56470I HERC01 LOGGED OFF TSO AT 14:32:00 ON MAY 28, 2026


z/OS V2R5   IP: 10.1.1.2

 ===> _
steps.expected: Logoff from TSO — identity is unbound, returning to anonymous VTAM session.
steps.hint: Never disconnect the terminal while logged in — it locks the userid. Recover with /C U=userid at the Hercules console. Three control planes were traversed: VTAM → TSO → ISPF.
